content:
Purpose / reminder
- This is the execution checklist for a controlled regional failover game day (staging first; production low-risk slice later). It is intentionally operational and terse.
- Primary goal: validate the automated failover trigger engine + orchestrator end-to-end (signals → trigger decision → safe-to-failover gates → progressive routing → rollback), while keeping blast radius tightly bounded.
- Secondary goal: validate comms + paging hygiene + audit trail.


0) Quick facts (fill in before the window)
- Date/time window:
- Environment: staging | prod
- Impaired region (source):
- Target region (destination):
- Routing scope: hosted | dedicated (which pools?)
- Traffic scope (must be explicit):
  - customer tiers:
  - routes/models:
  - canary % (start):
  - max % allowed:
- Trigger mode: monitor-only | auto-mitigate
- Orchestrator feature flag name + current state:
- Expected failover mechanism: internal routing policy change | edge/DNS change | both
- Test scenario ID(s) from test matrix:
- Change ticket / approval link:


1) Roles + responsibilities (confirm on the bridge)
- Incident Commander (IC): __________ (default: Rafael Mendes)
  - Owns go/no-go, stop conditions, timeline, and final call to rollback.
- Comms lead: __________ (default: Dev Patel for prod; Tomáš Novák for staging)
  - Owns internal updates, Support macros usage, and status-page decision path.
- SRE operator (orchestrator): __________ (default: Miles Thornton)
  - Executes flag changes, orchestrator actions, and captures audit links.
- Routing/operator (Smart Routing): __________ (default: Mina Haddad delegate)
  - Validates routing policy changes + confirms expected traffic movement.
- Infra/network operator: __________ (default: Victor Alvarez)
  - DNS/edge readiness, rollback, TTL constraints, confirms propagation behavior.
- Capacity operator: __________ (default: Harish Reddy)
  - Confirms headroom in target region; watches saturation and queue depths.
- Observability scribe: __________ (default: Aisha Bello or Sergio Costa)
  - Watches SLO/burn-rate/impact charts, timestamps key events, notes alert behavior.
- Observers (non-speaking unless requested): list names:

Checklist: everyone knows where the live coordination happens
- Primary channel: #incidents (thread: <link>)
- Secondary channel: #eng-sre + #eng-platform for side-questions
- Video/bridge: <link>
- Dashboards folder: <link>
- Runbook: Automated region failover runbook (Confluence)


2) Pre-flight (T-7 days to T-24 hours)
Approvals / change management
[ ] Confirm exec sponsor go-ahead if production (Neha Kapoor) and platform sign-off (Priya Natarajan or delegate).
[ ] Confirm release gating / required sign-offs completed (Connor O’Brien).
[ ] Confirm change window matches infra/networking constraints (no conflicting edge/DNS pushes).
[ ] Confirm rollback owner(s) and explicit rollback steps are documented (not “we’ll just undo it”).

Scope / blast radius
[ ] Confirm test matrix scenario and exact scope are selected (by tier/route/model).
[ ] Confirm max traffic % cap (hard limit) is configured (or enforced manually).
[ ] Confirm exclusions (enterprise allowlist/denylist; protected customers; internal traffic).

Safety gates
[ ] Safe-to-failover checks are enabled (capacity + dependency health + routing sanity checks).
[ ] Hold-down timers/hysteresis are configured to prevent flappy transitions.
[ ] Manual override permissions verified (RBAC group membership) for at least 2 people (primary + backup).
[ ] Confirm “monitor-only” available as an immediate fallback mode (no automated action).

Capacity readiness (destination region)
[ ] GPU pool headroom meets minimum: ________ (tokens/sec headroom OR % idle OR free GPUs)
[ ] Queue depth stable under baseline + expected added traffic.
[ ] Autoscaling policy understood for the window (avoid scaling surprises / cold-start impact).
[ ] Confirm dependency health in destination region: KV/cache, policy store, auth, telemetry ingestion, etc.

Observability readiness
[ ] Dashboards verified to load and show data for BOTH regions (source + destination).
[ ] Verify region health signals publishing (synthetic probes, error rate, tail latency, network path health).
[ ] Verify failover state machine panel shows current state (no stale state).
[ ] Burn-rate alerts are known; paging thresholds confirmed for game day (avoid “silent failures”).
[ ] Confirm we have a way to tag/annotate the timeline (deploy markers / manual annotations).

Comms readiness
[ ] Draft internal announcement prepared (what will happen, when, who to contact).
[ ] Support macro reviewed + ready (and a “do not proactively message customers” guidance unless approved).
[ ] Decide in advance if a public status-page update is allowed/required for prod tests (default: no, unless customer-visible impact exceeds agreed threshold).


3) Day-of pre-flight (T-90 min to T-5 min)
Room setup
[ ] Start bridge; confirm recording ON if required.
[ ] Start #incidents thread and pin: bridge, dashboards, runbook, scope, stop conditions.
[ ] Confirm all key roles present; assign backups.

System sanity checks (baseline)
[ ] Confirm baseline SLOs healthy (availability + p95/p99) for relevant routes.
[ ] Confirm region health is GREEN in both regions before beginning.
[ ] Confirm no ongoing incident/conflicting maintenance.
[ ] Confirm destination region capacity check passes NOW (not only “it passed earlier this week”).

Config + flags (do not proceed if unclear)
[ ] Confirm orchestrator and trigger engine build versions / deploy SHA (if applicable).
[ ] Confirm feature flag state(s):
    - trigger evaluation enabled?
    - auto-mitigate enabled?
    - progressive failover enabled?
    - audit logging enabled?
    - incident-bot posting enabled?
[ ] Confirm progressive failover “caps” and increments (e.g., 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% max) are configured.
[ ] Confirm rollback path is available at each stage (and tested in staging at least once).

Stop conditions (read aloud by IC; confirm everyone agrees)
- Stop condition A: customer-visible error rate exceeds ________ for > ________ minutes on scoped traffic.
- Stop condition B: destination region saturation (GPU, queue depth) exceeds ________ for > ________ minutes.
- Stop condition C: dependency health failure in destination region (policy store/auth/telemetry) persists > ________ minutes.
- Stop condition D: failover automation flaps (state transitions more than ____ times in ____ minutes) OR unexpected state.
- Stop condition E: any “unknown unknown” where we cannot explain behavior within ____ minutes.


4) Execution steps (staging first; prod follows same shape)
Important: At each step, scribe timestamps actions and resulting graphs/alerts.

Step 1 — Announce start
[ ] IC posts: starting controlled failover test; scope + max cap + stop conditions.
[ ] Comms lead posts FYI in #announcements (internal) if required.

Step 2 — Validate we can observe the trigger inputs
[ ] Synthetic probes visible for impaired region.
[ ] Error rate/latency panels show expected baseline.
[ ] Network path health panel visible (packet loss/RTT).
[ ] Confirm signal aggregation freshness (no >2–3 min lag).

Step 3 — Introduce impairment (per selected scenario)
Choose one; do not mix unless explicitly planned.
[ ] Scenario: elevated 5xx (how injected?):
[ ] Scenario: increased tail latency (how injected?):
[ ] Scenario: partial network impairment/packet loss (how injected?):
[ ] Scenario: capacity saturation (how simulated?):

[ ] Confirm impairment is actually happening in the source region (before expecting triggers).

Step 4 — Confirm trigger engine evaluation behavior
[ ] Trigger enters “suspect/degraded” (or equivalent) state with expected window.
[ ] Confirm hysteresis behavior: no immediate flip-flop.
[ ] Confirm alerting: expected alerts fire (or are suppressed) according to plan.
[ ] Confirm audit trail entry exists for evaluation (link).

Step 5 — Confirm safe-to-failover gates
[ ] Destination region capacity check passes.
[ ] Destination dependency checks pass.
[ ] Routing policy sanity check passes (no invalid policy diff).
[ ] If any gate fails, document which gate + why; do not proceed to traffic movement.

Step 6 — Progressive failover (traffic movement)
Start at smallest canary.
[ ] Move 1% of scoped traffic to destination region.
    - Verify: traffic shift observable in routing metrics.
    - Verify: error rate/latency for canary segment within bounds.
    - Verify: destination queue depth stable.
[ ] Hold for ____ minutes.
[ ] Increase to 5% (or next planned step).
[ ] Hold for ____ minutes.
[ ] Increase to 25% (optional; only if prior steps clean).
[ ] Hold for ____ minutes.
[ ] Increase to max cap (only if explicitly approved in this run).

At each increment, validate:
[ ] Scoped customer impact panel (by tier) shows expected behavior.
[ ] Streaming disconnect rate (if applicable) is within expected bounds.
[ ] No unexpected cross-region routing for excluded tiers/customers.
[ ] Audit log includes state transition + actor (automation/manual) + reason.
[ ] Incident-bot message appears in #incidents with correct state + links.

Step 7 — Stabilize and observe “degraded but available” behavior
[ ] Confirm load shedding policy behaves as expected (if enabled).
[ ] Confirm fallback model variant selection behaves as expected (if part of scope).
[ ] Confirm timeouts/queue tuning applied only to scoped traffic.

Step 8 — Rollback / recovery
Rollback criteria (choose one):
- Impairment removed and region health returns to normal; OR
- We validated intended behavior sufficiently; OR
- Stop condition triggered.

[ ] Begin rollback to normal routing.
[ ] Confirm traffic returns to primary region OR policy returns to steady-state.
[ ] Confirm no lingering forced routing for scoped customers.
[ ] Confirm hold-down timer behavior (no immediate re-triggering after rollback).
[ ] Remove impairment.
[ ] Confirm health signals return to GREEN.


5) Comms checklist (internal + Support/CS)
Internal updates cadence (recommended)
[ ] T0: start notice in #incidents (scope + stop conditions)
[ ] At each major state transition: suspected → degraded → failover_in_progress → partial_failover → rollback
[ ] If any unexpected alert/paging: acknowledge and explain whether expected

Support coordination (prod only; staging as-needed)
[ ] Confirm Support on-call aware of window.
[ ] Confirm macro to use if customers ask: controlled test; potential brief latency/route changes; no action needed.
[ ] Confirm escalation path for enterprise: Support → SRE on-call → IC.

Status page
[ ] Default: do not post for low-risk slice unless customer-visible impact exceeds pre-agreed threshold.
[ ] If posting is needed: use “Performance Degradation (Investigating)” template; avoid mentioning “test” publicly unless explicitly approved.


6) Paging + alert hygiene
[ ] Confirm paging routes will reach correct on-call (no stale rotations).
[ ] Confirm at least one person has permissions to silence non-actionable alerts during the window (and documents each silence).
[ ] Confirm we do NOT globally silence region health alerts (we need to see what would happen in reality).
[ ] Record which alerts fired, which didn’t, and which were noisy.


7) Post-flight validation (immediately after rollback)
Traffic + correctness
[ ] Traffic distribution returns to expected steady-state (verify for 30–60 minutes).
[ ] No residual routing policy overrides remain.
[ ] Confirm no “stuck” failover state in orchestrator.

SLO/SLA impact
[ ] SLO panels: availability and latency within normal bounds post-test.
[ ] Error budget burn: confirm any burn event matches expectations and is scoped.

Capacity and performance
[ ] Destination region utilization returns to baseline (no leaked autoscaling state).
[ ] Queue depths normalize.

Observability + audit trail
[ ] Audit log entries are complete for: trigger evaluation, gate checks, state transitions, manual overrides (if any).
[ ] Incident timeline in #incidents has key timestamps and links to graphs.
[ ] Save screenshots/links for before/after panels in the retro doc.

Customer checks (prod only)
[ ] Scan for SUP tickets created during the window.
[ ] Ask Support if any customers noticed or escalated.


8) Retro + follow-ups (within 24–72 hours)
[ ] Create/update retro notes using post-test analysis template.
[ ] File issues for:
    - false positives/negatives in triggers
    - missing/laggy signals
    - safe-to-failover gate gaps
    - routing scoping bugs
    - alert noise / missing alerts
    - runbook ambiguity
[ ] Update thresholds/hysteresis proposal (if needed) and route to ADR owner.
[ ] If this was staging: decide readiness for production low-risk slice and list remaining blockers.


Appendix A — Minimal dashboard list (paste actual links day-of)
- Region health overview (errors, p95/p99, dependency health):
- Network path health (probe RTT/packet loss):
- Failover orchestrator state machine + audit log:
- Traffic distribution by region for scoped routes/models:
- Capacity: GPU utilization + headroom + queue depth:
- Customer impact by tier:
- Error budget burn-rate alert panels:


Appendix B — Notes to self / open questions (keep short; convert to follow-ups)
- TTL constraints: are we relying on DNS changes for this scenario? If yes, confirm expected propagation timeline and how we measure it.
- If triggers misbehave: do we switch to monitor-only, or force manual progressive failover? (IC must decide quickly.)
- Dedicated customers: confirm whether they are included/excluded for this run; if included, confirm dedicated pool headroom separately.
